note: HUMAN-GROUNDED positional corpus. Every entry exists because a reputable human source
explicitly named the concept for this position — never because an engine liked a move.
The division of labour is the point, and it is recorded per entry:
the CONCEPT and its explanation come from the human annotation;
Stockfish verifies only whether the annotated move is sound, what it prefers,
and whether the positional claim survives concrete calculation.
engine.agrees is therefore a FINDING, not a filter. An annotated move the engine
does not choose is kept, because the concept can be sound while the move is not,
and that distinction is exactly what a learner needs and what an engine-labelled
fen_verified records how the position was obtained. 'replay' means the whole game
was played through the page's own move generator, so the FEN is derived rather than
transcribed. Two game scores from reputable sources have already failed that check.

alternate_concepts_considered was originally one list, and the stress test showed why that was wrong: it lumped concepts that are ALSO TRUE but secondary together with concepts that would be WRONG here. Reporting the first is correct behaviour and reporting the second is a false positive, so they are now separate fields and only rejected_as_wrong counts against the system.

fen_concept_realised exists for entries where the concept only appears after a FORCED reply. 9.Nxc6 creates a doubled isolated pawn, and it does so after Black recaptures; asking about the position between the two halves of the exchange is asking before the concept exists.

concept_roles.positive: the concept clearly applies, on the annotator's authority
concept_roles.negative: the board superficially resembles the concept and it should NOT be labelled that way
concept_roles.ambiguous: the concept contributes but is not clearly the primary explanation

positions.annotator: Nicholas Van Der Nat (Chess.com), following the classical literature
positions.fen_verified: replay: all 77 plies replayed legally through blind-chess.html's move generator
positions.human_annotation: 'The critical moment comes at move 9 when Rubinstein plays 9.Nxc6!, trading the knight to give Black a doubled, isolated c-pawn. Black now has two problems: a weak d-pawn AND a weak c-pawn.'
positions.explanation: The concept applies because the capture MANUFACTURES the second weakness rather than exploiting an existing one. Before it Black has one target, the isolated d5 pawn; after it Black has two, on c6 and d5, and they cannot both be defended by pawns. This base's own detector confirms the structural claim: after 9...bxc6 Black's pawns stand on a, c, c, d, f, g, h with three islands.

engine.agrees: substantially — the annotated move is the engine's second choice, 0.05 behind its first
engine.note: The engine marginally prefers 9.Nb5. A five-hundredth of a pawn is not a disagreement about the plan, and the structural consequence the annotator describes is not in doubt.

positions.why_not_alternates: doubled-pawns and the isolated pawn are the RESULT and are recorded separately; what makes this two-weaknesses is that a second, separated target is created on purpose. piece-exchanges describes the mechanism, not the aim.
positions.fen_after_note: The position the annotated move reaches. A move-based concept describes what the move ACHIEVES, so the checker looks here as well as at the position before it.
positions.fen_concept_realised_note: After 9.Nxc6 bxc6, the forced recapture. The doubled isolated c-pawn the annotation is about exists only here.

positions.annotator: Nicholas Van Der Nat (Chess.com), following the classical literature
positions.fen_verified: replay: all 77 plies replayed legally through blind-chess.html's move generator
positions.human_annotation: 'After patient maneuvering, Rubinstein plays the instructive 20.e3! This seemingly small move accomplishes a great deal: it gains a tempo by attacking Black's queen, opens a diagonal for the bishop, and clears the second rank so the rook can swing from f2 to c2, doubling on the c-file.'
positions.explanation: A quiet move whose entire purpose is to improve the pieces that are doing least — the f1 bishop, shut in, and the f2 rook, off the file that matters. The concept's condition is satisfied exactly: nothing urgent is happening, so the right move is the one that improves the worst-placed piece.

engine.agrees: yes — the annotated move is the engine's first choice
engine.note: A rare clean agreement between a century-old annotation and a modern engine on a quiet move.

positions.why_not_alternates: semi-open-file names where the rook is going and not why this move is right. prophylaxis was rejected: nothing of Black's is being prevented, White's own pieces are being improved, which is the distinction the two records exist to keep apart.
positions.fen_after_note: The position the annotated move reaches. A move-based concept describes what the move ACHIEVES, so the checker looks here as well as at the position before it.

positions.annotator: Nicholas Van Der Nat (Chess.com), following the classical literature
positions.fen_verified: replay: all 77 plies replayed legally through blind-chess.html's move generator
positions.human_annotation: 'Now Rubinstein plays 24.b4!, the decisive pawn break. The immediate threat is 25.b5, attacking the immobilized c-pawn a third time. Black is forced to play 24...a6, creating yet another weakness: the a6-pawn.'
positions.explanation: The human claim is that the pawn break forces a THIRD target into existence on a6, stretching a defence already tied to c6 and d5. The concept is well attested here; the MOVE is not the engine's.

engine.agrees: NO — the engine plays 22.Rb2 at +4.24 and does not rank the annotated move in its top three, all of which are at most +1.52
engine.note: Recorded as a disagreement rather than resolved. The strategic idea the annotation describes is real and the game bears it out, and the engine sees a much stronger continuation that the annotator does not mention. Both are true. This is why concept_role here is AMBIGUOUS: the concept contributes and is not the whole explanation of why the position is winning.

positions.why_not_alternates: minority-attack was considered and rejected — this is not a Carlsbad structure and White is not advancing a minority into a majority. pawn-breaks describes the move; two-weaknesses describes its purpose.
positions.fen_after_note: The position the annotated move reaches. A move-based concept describes what the move ACHIEVES, so the checker looks here as well as at the position before it.
